name: Grail

attributes.attribute: sacred cup of the Last Supper
sometimes the platter for the paschal lamb
carried to Britain by Joseph of Arimathea
wounded king healed only when the quest completes

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Holy Grail is a symbolic object pictured as the sacred cup Jesus drank from at the Last Supper. Some tellings describe it as the platter for his bread or the paschal lamb. Others say it caught his blood as he lay dying. Joseph of Arimathea, the merchant who owned the supper house, carried the Grail to Britain. The Christian emblem of transubstantiation then fused with Celtic legends into a complex tale that still moves poets and thinkers. In that tale the Fisher King lies wounded in his body and heals only when the quest is complete.

okr.objective: Describe the Holy Grail's forms, its journey to Britain, and its wounded-king quest.
key_results: The Grail is shown as the sacred cup of the Last Supper.
Joseph of Arimathea carried the Grail to Britain.
The Christian emblem fused with Celtic legends into a rich tale.
The Fisher King heals only when the Grail quest is complete.
